newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH sees 1997 EPS dilution from DFS buy.
newsitem.headline: LVMH sees 1997 EPS dilution from DFS buy.

text.p: Luxury goods conglomerate LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton said on Thursday that it expected the acquisition of U.S. duty free chain DFS to have a dilutive effect in 1997 on its earnings per share.
"The objective set for LVMH in 1997 is for a new increase in sales and profits before the impact of the DFS acquisition," the company said in a statement of its provisional 1996 sales.

"LVMH recalls that the acquisition should lead to growth on the order of 50 percent for sales and close to 30 percent for LVMH's operating profit. It should have a positive impact on the operating profit (after taxes and before goodwill writeoff)," it said in a statement.
But it said the impact would be dilutive. A spokeswoman for LVMH told Reuters the acquisition would result in lower earnings per share in 1997.
LVMH has bought 61.25 percent of DFS for around $2.6 billion after concluding a deal with the majority holders of DFS last year.
It said in its statement that the acquisition would generate "significant cashflow".
